body:
By the way this was an absolute hell to track down, because of how `custom_data` and tilemap collisions seemed like absolutely unrelated topics to me ;) . So if Godot exhibits some magic action at a distance here, I think it could be a good idea to consider contributions that simplify the tilemap code, because this is the kind of weird interaction that shouldn't "just happen".

_However_, I assume this might be because collision boxes are themselves stored as custom data inside tilemaps...? I didn't have time to look into the tilemap code in detail, but my guess is that writing values to `custom_data` dirties the collision boxes, so the physics server has to re-add them, and the `Area2D` doesn't like that somehow? That would make the bug a lot less weird to me.

What might also help in tracking down this issue: **If I modify the TileMap's script in the MRP to use _`physics_process()` instead of `_process()`, the collision detection works.** This is still a pretty nasty bug, obviously, but this might be a good workaround for some users.

Following the signal rabbit hole:
`TileData::set_custom_data()`emits "changed" which eventually ends up in `TileMapLayer::_tile_set_changed()` where it queues a recompute of everything that depends on the tileset (including all the physics shapes). The physics bodies need to be valid for one frame and synced between threads before intersection callbacks can happen iirc, so they never do unless two physics ticks happen back to back in the MRP (you can trigger this by increasing the game-speed). So this doesn't seem like a bug to me, just not very well documented behaviour. Doing the custom data operation in physics_process seems like a reasonable thing here for now.

Though there is also room for improvement imo. Recomputing all of this data for every custom_data_layer change seems wasteful, so maybe adding a flag to the data_layer on whether changes should mark the entire TileSet dirty and more fine grained dirty rects would be good.

Thank you for the research :). That confirms my suspicions.

Imo this is definitely a bug and not a documentation issue. Even if we documented it, we've now promoted a corner case to a "feature", which adds complexity to the code base and to understanding Godot. It also restricts the user to setting custom_data only inside physics_process for games that care about physics.

It sounds like we could resolve the issue by tracking which custom_data layer and tile has changed, when we write custom_data. That should be a good performance improvement anyway, because atm all writes to custom_data interact with the physics server.
